notes_for_editor: Fact-checked 2026-10-27. (1) Thin station: no keepers, storms, wrecks or rescues are sourced for this pier. (2) Height: LighthouseFriends and the CCG entry both give 8.5 m; the station file gives 9.0 m (its own source, not read). Not resolved. (3) CCG List of Lights entry (read on the cached page): Port Borden Pier, On outer end of Ferry Pier, Iso G 4s, 'White octagonal tower with red top', 8.5 m, Seasonal. The story states both the octagonal and hexagonal descriptions and the seasonal marking; the sources do not show which is current. The range figure in the CCG entry is not used because its unit is not printed in the extract. (4) 1918 'New Aids' entry: Port Borden, the erection of range lights and reflectors, $1,204.97 (1,204 97 in OCR); name and figure checked on the page image (scan p. 31, printed p. 32). (5) 1921 entry: the printed name is 'Fort Bordon' (checked on the page image, scan p. 33, printed p. 26); the story says the entry is evidently Port Borden, not stated by the report. (6) The 1976 date and the 1997 end of ferry service rest on LighthouseFriends; the French Wikipedia lead is not cited. (7) The station file's CCG number A1017.1 versus the CCG entry 1017.5 was not resolved and is not used. (8) The station file's 2012 Registered Heritage Place entry and PEI Register 8230 were not checked. (9) LighthouseFriends quotations shortened or paraphrased for copyright; the 1918 and 1921 report quotations are public domain.
